title: Config & Secrets
summary: Separate configuration from images the Kubernetes way: ConfigMaps and Secrets consumed as env vars or files, what actually updates at runtime, why base64 is not security, encryption at rest, rolling restarts on config change, and the external secret managers used in production.
objectives: Create ConfigMaps and Secrets from literals, files and env files, and consume them with env, envFrom and volumes
Predict which consumption methods pick up changes at runtime (mounted files) and which never do (env vars, subPath)
Explain why Secrets are only base64-encoded, how encryption at rest works, and how RBAC protects them
Combine sources with projected volumes and expose pod metadata with the downward API
Apply 12-factor config to a NestJS/Node service with validation at startup
Trigger rolling restarts on config change with hashes, checksum annotations or `kubectl rollout restart`
Compare External Secrets Operator, Sealed Secrets, SOPS and the Secrets Store CSI driver
